answer.note: All four ref files contain the same generic text, so they gave me no file-specific priority. I chose the refs by reading the code. C (visibility.py) is the best match. It has three arms (codeword, public, explicit). Its receive() at lines 141-188 resumes a checkpoint after checking the registration hash, preregistration commit, command and trial order. It writes a private ledger.json and a public file containing the ledger digest. B (heldout.py) is the closest comparison. It has the same receive/checkpoint/public-digest pattern and also checks the sender seal, but it hard-codes 180 trials and has no ARMS constant, so I didn't confirm it has three arms. D (honest.py) has only two arms, so it doesn't fit. A (study.py) has the same receive pattern but no ARMS constant. Suggested 60-minute split: about 35 minutes on C, 15 on B, 5 each on A and D to rule them out. The handoff's two refs (B and C) turned out to be the right pair, but I picked them on the code, not on the handoff. I only read visibility.py lines 141-200 in full and grepped the others, so the split rests on that.

input.note: All four ref files contain the same generic text, so they gave me no file-specific priority. I chose the refs by reading the code. C (visibility.py) is the best match. It has three arms (codeword, public, explicit). Its receive() at lines 141-188 resumes a checkpoint after checking the registration hash, preregistration commit, command and trial order. Suggested 60-minute split: about 35 minutes on C, 15 on B, 5 each on A and D to rule them out. The handoff's two refs (B and C) turned out to be the right pair, but I picked them on the code, not on the handoff. I only read visibility.py lines 141-200 in full and grepped the others, so the split rests on that.
